Review Rooms?

Rooms has received overwhelmingly positive feedback for its creative and interactive platform. Users appreciate its versatility, allowing them to create and explore unique spaces, reminiscent of a more mature Minecraft. The platform's ease of use, even for those without prior coding experience, is highlighted, with Lua scripting enabling deep customization. Reviewers commend the polished experience and the potential for educational use, particularly in teaching coding. The community-driven aspect excites users, who are eager to see the innovative creations that emerge. Overall, Rooms is celebrated for its engaging and imaginative environment.

Played around with Rooms a bunch as a "consumer" of rooms and frankly, haven't had such a delightful experience with a game-like product for a while. The overall experience is incredibly polished, I love clicking through and finding easter eggs, and some of the game-oriented rooms are genuinely fun and addicting. Personally - I'm excited/curious to see how this evolves. Think it would be an awesome game for kids to help them learn how to code and build worlds a-la Minecraft, or (selfishly) I want to see more games and puzzles built out so I have more to play!

Review Hopper?

Reviewers are overwhelmingly negative on Hopper as a booking service. The recurring complaints are failed reservations, bait-and-switch room or flight details, canceled or changed bookings, and long refund fights even when hotels or airlines approved them. Customer support is described as hard to reach, slow, scripted, and sometimes gated behind paid tiers, leaving users bounced between Hopper and travel providers. A small note of praise appears for price prediction and occasional successful bookings, but reviewers say the app becomes unreliable and costly as soon as anything goes wrong.
